findings.body: totalPages is computed as floor(count/limit)+1, one more than the real number of pages, so currentPage never equals totalPages, showingLast stays false, the 'next' control stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to an empty member page.
findings.failure_mode: Incorrect pagination arithmetic yields an extra navigable but empty page and breaks the showingLast/next disabling logic.
findings.impact: totalPages is computed as floor(count/limit)+1, one more than the real number of pages, so currentPage never equals totalPages, showingLast stays false, the 'next' control stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to an empty member page.
findings.root_cause: Pagination total was implemented with floor(...)+1 instead of ceil(...), which overcounts when the count divides evenly by the limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (returning 0 only when user_count is 0) so an evenly divisible count yields the correct page total.
findings.title: totalPages off-by-one produces a spurious empty last page
findings.trigger: A group whose member count is an exact multiple of the page limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50, or 100 with limit 50).
findings.verifier_reason: Line 13 verbatim shows `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For user_count=50, limit=50, this yields floor(1)+1=2 instead of ceil(1)=1. currentPage maxes at 1, so showingLast (currentPage==totalPages) is false, next stays enabled, navigating to empty page 2.

raw_findings.body: Inside the group-member item view the template context is the individual User, which has no `automatic` property, so `{{#unless automatic}}` is always truthy and the remove (times) link is shown even for automatic-group members; clicking it fires removeMember, which the server rejects with 422.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Property lookup silently resolves to undefined in the child view context, defeating the intended conditional.
raw_findings.impact: Inside the group-member item view the template context is the individual User, which has no `automatic` property, so `{{#unless automatic}}` is always truthy and the remove (times) link is shown even for automatic-group members; clicking it fires removeMember, which the server rejects with 422.
raw_findings.root_cause: The remove link relies on `automatic`, but in the per-member item view that identifier resolves against the member record rather than the group model.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the group's automatic flag into the item view (e.g. bind it explicitly) or gate the remove link at the parent template where `automatic` resolves to the group.
raw_findings.title: Remove link rendered for automatic-group members because `automatic` is out of scope in item view
raw_findings.trigger: Viewing an automatic group in the admin group screen, where the member list is rendered via the group-member item view.

finding.title: Remove link rendered for automatic-group members because `automatic` is out of scope in item view
finding.trigger: Viewing an automatic group in the admin group screen, where the member list is rendered via the group-member item view.
finding.verifier_reason: The template is new and uses `{{#unless automatic}}`. The claim assumes `automatic` is out of scope, but Ember's ObjectController proxies model properties, so if the parent group model has `automatic` (confirmed in BasicGroupSerializer), it resolves correctly. No evidence the context is the User model; the view is rendered via `itemView` which inherits controller context.
